title: Branching Strategies for Teams —

header.html: Compare trunk-based development, GitHub flow and Git Flow; choose a strategy for a team; run release branches and hotfixes; name branches well; explain the cost of long-lived branches; tag releases with semantic versions; read git describe; know what a GitHub release is
Git 2.50.1 for the local parts; the GitHub documentation (read 2026-11-16) for the GitHub parts

toc.title: Three strategies and the team each one fits

html:
1Three strategies and the team each one fits

A branching strategy is the team's agreement on which branches exist, how long they live and how work reaches users. The figure compares three common ones.

Strategy Branches How work reaches users
Trunk-based main plus branches that live hours or a day or two Small changes merge to main at once; feature flags hide unfinished work
GitHub flow main plus one short branch per change Pull request, review, merge, deploy from main
Git Flow main, develop, feature, release, hotfix Features go to develop, a release branch stabilizes, main holds releases

In trunk-based development the rule is small changes, merged often. A feature flag is a setting that the code checks, so unfinished code can sit in main while switched off. In the demo, a new checkout ships behind new_checkout=off, then a one-line change turns it on.

GitHub flow is the six steps of module 9, and main is always ready to deploy.

Git Flow gives every branch a job:

Branch Job Starts from Merges into
main Released code; every release gets a tag The first commit Nothing
develop Integration of the next release main main, through a release
feature/ One feature develop develop
release/ Stabilize a release: version bump, last fixes develop main and develop
hotfix/ Urgent fix to released code main main and develop

Try it. After one full cycle (feature, release, hotfix), main shows only releases. Your hashes will differ.

git log --oneline --first-parent main
git tag
git describe --tags main

b3e38b9 Merge hotfix/1.1.1
0d6c513 Merge release/1.1.0
188a95e Add README
v1.0.0
v1.1.0
v1.1.1
v1.1.1
Team Best fit
Small team, strong automated tests, deploys many times a day Trunk-based
Web app deployed from main, every change reviewed in a PR GitHub flow
Scheduled releases and several supported versions Git Flow or release branches
Tip

. Start with GitHub flow and add complexity only when a real need appears. Every extra long-lived branch is more merging.

2Release branches and hotfixes

A release branch such as release/1.2 is cut from the release tag and stays alive while that version is supported. A hotfix repairs a bug found in a shipped version. It takes three moves:

  1. Branch hotfix/rounding from release/1.2, and commit the fix.
  2. Merge it into release/1.2 with --no-ff, and tag v1.2.1.
  3. Copy the fix to main with git cherry-pick -x, which records the source commit in the message.

One bug means one fix on every line that has it. In Git Flow the hotfix goes into main and develop.

Try it. Fix a shipped version and carry the fix to main.

git switch -c hotfix/rounding release/1.2
echo "round=half-up" > total.txt
git commit -am "Fix rounding in the cart total"
git switch release/1.2
git merge --no-ff hotfix/rounding -m "Merge hotfix/rounding into release/1.2"
git tag -a v1.2.1 -m "Hotfix: rounding"
git switch main
git cherry-pick -x hotfix/rounding
git log -1 --format=%B
git describe --tags release/1.2
git describe --tags main

Fix rounding in the cart total

(cherry picked from commit 40eee3b8c2a54c8f71b689f3fda7c2206d87169c)
v1.2.1
v1.2.0-3-gcf09be3

The copy on main is a new commit with a new hash. Two results can surprise you. git describe on main still counts from v1.2.0, because v1.2.1 is not reachable from main. And git branch -d hotfix/rounding refuses on main, because the hotfix commit itself is not in main. Delete it while on release/1.2.

Tip

. Use git cherry-pick -x when you copy a fix. The "cherry picked from" line lets anyone trace the copy back to the original.

3Branch names and long-lived branches

Keep names short, lowercase and descriptive, with a prefix for the purpose.

Prefix Use Sample
feature/ New work feature/123-cart-totals
fix/ Ordinary bug fix fix/login-redirect
hotfix/ Urgent production fix hotfix/rounding
release/ Release preparation or support release/1.2

Git refuses spaces and .. in a name. It also refuses a branch named feature while feature/cart exists, because branches are stored as paths: the error is cannot lock ref.

A long-lived branch drifts away from main. Every day it costs more: conflicts grow, reviews get bigger, and nobody else sees the work. Measure the drift and test the merge early.

Try it. Count how far apart two branches are, then try the merge.

git rev-list --left-right --count main...redesign
git merge redesign
git merge --abort

4	1
Auto-merging ui.txt
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in ui.txt
Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.

The numbers are commits only in main (4) and only in the branch (1). The cure: merge main in often, cut the work into small PRs, and hide unfinished work behind flags. Release branches are long-lived on purpose, but take fixes only.

4Tags, versions and releases

A tag is a permanent name for one commit. An annotated tag stores the tagger, the date and a message, so use it for releases. A lightweight tag is only a name; git cat-file -t prints tag for the first kind and commit for the second.

A plain git push sends branches, not tags. Send one tag with git push origin v1.2.0, or all with --tags. A fresh clone then has them.

git describe --tags names a commit from the nearest tag. On the tag it prints the tag. Two commits later it prints v1.2.0-2-g717b871: the tag, the commits since it, and g plus the short hash.

Try it. Tag a release, describe it before and after two more commits, and push it.

git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "Gift cards"
git describe --tags
# two more commits later
git describe --tags
git push origin v1.2.0

v1.2.0
v1.2.0-2-g717b871
 * [new tag]         v1.2.0 -> v1.2.0

Semantic versioning writes versions as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, and a lower number resets when a higher one rises.

Number Rises when Sample
MAJOR A breaking change forces users to adapt 1.2.3 becomes 2.0.0
MINOR A new feature that stays backward compatible 1.2.3 becomes 1.3.0
PATCH A backward compatible bug fix 1.2.3 becomes 1.2.4

A plain git tag sorts by name, so v1.10.0 appears before v1.2.0. Sort by version instead.

Try it. List three tags by name, then by version.

git tag
git tag --sort=v:refname

v1.10.0
v1.2.0
v1.9.0
v1.2.0
v1.9.0
v1.10.0

A GitHub release is based on a Git tag. Managing releases needs write permission. The notes can be written by hand or generated from a template, and GitHub attaches the source as a ZIP file and a tarball. A release can hold up to 1000 assets, each under 2 GiB.

Tip

. Tag every release with an annotated tag, and push it by name. Releases, git describe and rollbacks all depend on tags that really exist.

5Practice Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Ada's team deploys main many times a day. A new checkout is unfinished, but its first pieces should merge now. What lets them do it safely?

  • AKeep everything on one branch until the checkout is finished
  • BMerge the code behind a feature flag that is switched off
  • CTag the unfinished code as a pre-release before merging it
  • DMerge the code into a release branch and leave out main
Show the answer

Answer: B. A feature flag lets unfinished code live in main without users seeing it.

S2A bug is reported in the shipped v1.2.0, and main already holds 1.3 work. Where does the fix belong?

  • AOnly on main, and then customers receive all of the 1.3 work
  • BOnly on release/1.2, because main picks it up by itself
  • COn a new branch from develop, then tag v1.2.0 once more
  • DOn a branch from release/1.2, tag v1.2.1, then copy to main
Show the answer

Answer: D. Fix the supported line first, tag it, and copy the fix to every other line that has the bug.

S3git describe --tags prints v1.4.0-3-g9a1b2c3. What does that tell you?

  • AHEAD is three commits after the tag v1.4.0, at commit 9a1b2c3
  • BThree tags named v1.4.0 exist, and the newest is 9a1b2c3
  • CThe tag v1.4.0 points at the third commit of the branch
  • DThe branch is three commits behind the remote copy of main
Show the answer

Answer: A. The format is the tag, the commits since it, and g plus the short hash.

S4The shop is at 2.3.4. A release removes a function that other teams call. Which version comes next?

  • A2.3.5, because it is only one more fix on 2.3
  • B2.4.0, because it is a change to the feature set
  • C3.0.0, because a breaking change raises MAJOR
  • D3.3.4, because the first number rises by one
Show the answer

Answer: C. A breaking change raises MAJOR and resets MINOR and PATCH to 0.

S5Bob tagged v2.0.0 and ran git push. Teammates cannot see the tag on GitHub. What is the fix?

  • ARun git push --force so that GitHub accepts the new tags
  • BRun git push origin v2.0.0, as a plain push sends no tags
  • CRecreate the tag as a lightweight tag with the plain git tag
  • DAsk an admin to make the tag visible to the whole team
Show the answer

Answer: B. A plain git push sends branches only, so the tag must be pushed by name.

S6A team ships packaged software on a schedule and supports versions 1.x and 2.x at the same time. Which approach fits best?

  • ATrunk-based development with no release branches at all
  • BGitHub flow with one branch per change and no tags
  • COne long-lived feature branch kept for each supported customer
  • DRelease branches per version, tagged, with hotfixes to each
Show the answer

Answer: D. Several supported versions need a branch and tags for each, and a hotfix for each affected line.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Name the five branch types of Git Flow.

Show the answer

main, develop, feature, release and hotfix.

R2When does the MINOR number rise?

Show the answer

When a backward compatible feature is added; PATCH resets to 0.

R3Which command creates an annotated tag?

Show the answer

git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "message".

R4Which command sends one tag to the remote?

Show the answer

git push origin v1.2.0.

R5What is a GitHub release based on?

Show the answer

A Git tag.

R6Which command shows how far a branch has drifted from main?

Show the answer

git rev-list --left-right --count, run on main...branch.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Trunk-based tiny branches, merge often, feature flags hide unfinished work
GitHub flow one short branch per change, PR, merge, deploy from main
Git Flow main, develop, feature, release, hotfix; releases tagged on main
Hotfix branch from the release, merge and tag, then git cherry-pick -x to main
Branch names prefix and short description; no spaces; feature clashes with feature/cart
Long-lived branches drift and conflicts; measure with git rev-list --left-right --count
Tags git tag -a, then git push origin TAG; a plain push sends none
Semantic versions MAJOR breaking, MINOR feature, PATCH fix
describe tag-N-ghash means N commits after the tag
GitHub release based on a tag; notes by hand or template; source ZIP and tarball added
